idiom_name: Object.freeze (shallow) + spread copy-on-write updates + structuredClone for deep copies
implementation_notes: JavaScript objects and arrays are mutable and const only prevents rebinding, so immutability is a discipline: Object.freeze returns the same object with its own properties made non-writable and non-configurable (writes fail silently in sloppy mode and throw a TypeError in strict mode or module code), but it is shallow - nested objects and arrays stay mutable unless every level is frozen. The idiomatic replacement for an immutable object with setters is copy-on-write updating with spread or Object.assign, plus a persistent-collections library (Immutable.js) or a producer library (Immer) where structural sharing matters; structuredClone produces a deep mutable copy and therefore complements immutability at boundaries rather than providing it. The classic hand-written immutable wrapper is still justified for a module's public state object: freeze it once at construction and expose update functions only.
pitfalls: Object.freeze is shallow: freezing the top object leaves nested objects and arrays mutable, which is the classic accidental-mutation bug in redux-style stores.
A write to a frozen object fails silently in sloppy mode and throws only in strict mode or modules, so the same bug can pass unnoticed in one file and throw in another.
Spread and Object.assign copies are shallow too: nested references stay shared, so an update that mutates a nested object mutates the previous version as well.
Freezing typed arrays throws a TypeError (array buffer views cannot be frozen), and freezing interacts badly with proxies and accessor properties.
